events.title: Southern Taurids near their peak
events.detail: Occasional bright meteors are possible from a dark Cincinnati-area site. Look across a broad sky after dark; this is a low-rate shower, not a meteor storm.

events.title: Northern Taurids near their peak
events.detail: A few meteors and occasional fireballs may be visible. Dark skies and an unobstructed view matter more than looking at one exact spot.

events.title: Mars and Jupiter close before sunrise
events.detail: Look southeast before dawn for Jupiter with reddish Mars nearby. NASA lists an apparent separation of about 1.2 degrees. A clear horizon is needed.

events.title: Leonid viewing window before dawn
events.detail: NASA recommends the early morning after moonset. Cincinnati-area light pollution and clouds can reduce what you see; ideal-sky rates are not a local forecast.

events.title: Full supermoon
events.detail: Look east near sunset for the rising full Moon. Its apparent size difference is modest. The selected date’s moonrise and phase information appear alongside this guide.
